title: Robot-Assisted Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy (da Vinci) versus Conventional Total Laparoscopic Hysterectomy: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Both Surgical Techniques
summary:
Background:

Removal of the uterus is one of the most commonly performed operations in gynecology. It may be necessary for various non-cancerous conditions, such as heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding, benign growths in the uterus, or chronic pain. Nowadays, the uterus can often be removed through small incisions in the abdomen. Two surgical approaches are available: conventional keyhole surgery, in which the surgeon directly controls the surgical instruments, and robot-assisted surgery, in which the instruments are controlled using a computer-assisted system. Both methods are already established. However, it remains unclear whether one approach offers advantages over the other in terms of surgical outcomes, recovery, and quality of life.

Research Question:

The aim of this study is to compare the two surgical approaches and investigate whether robot-assisted surgery is at least as safe and effective as conventional keyhole surgery. The study will examine potential differences in the duration of surgery, the frequency of complications, blood loss, postoperative pain, length of hospital stay, and recovery. In addition, patients' quality of life and satisfaction after surgery will be assessed. The study will also investigate how surgeons' experience and surgical outcomes develop over time when performing robot-assisted procedures.

Methods:

A total of 240 adult women who are scheduled to undergo removal of the uterus due to a non-cancerous condition will be enrolled at the Department of Gynecology of Städtisches Klinikum Karlsruhe, Germany. After receiving detailed information about the study and providing written consent, participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. In 120 women, the uterus will be removed using robot-assisted surgery, while the other 120 women will undergo conventional keyhole surgery.

During and after the operation, various data will be collected, including the duration of surgery, possible complications, blood loss, the need for pain medication, and the length of hospital stay. In addition, routinely recorded information on the time and materials required for both surgical approaches will be evaluated.

Six and twelve months after surgery, participants will be contacted by telephone and asked standardized questions about their quality of life, satisfaction, return to everyday activities, and ability to return to work.

All collected information will be treated confidentially and analyzed in a way that prevents direct identification of individual patients. Participation is voluntary, and participants may withdraw from the study at any time without affecting their future medical care.
conditions: Benign gynecological conditions requiring hysterectomy, particularly uterine fibroids, abnormal uterine bleeding, endometriosis, adenomyosis, and endometrial or cervical abnormalities. The study compares robot-assisted total laparoscopic hysterectomy with conventional total laparoscopic hysterectomy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female patients older than 18 years.

Indication for hysterectomy due to a benign gynecological condition, including uterine fibroids, heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding, endometriosis, uterine adenomyosis, and endometrial or cervical hyperplasia and/or atypia.

Written informed consent to participate in the study following comprehensive patient information.

Consent to the collection and scientific analysis of study-related data.

Consent to telephone follow-up interviews at 6 and 12 months postoperatively.
Exclusion criteria:
Malignant disease of the uterus, particularly endometrial carcinoma or uterine sarcoma.

Inability to provide informed consent.

Absence of written informed consent for study participation.

Failure to meet one or more of the inclusion criteria.
